name: fine- to medium-grained sand beach
oil_penetration_depth: about 10-15 cm in fine- to medium-grained sand
burial_risk: rapid: within one day; to about 1 m if oil comes ashore at the start of a depositional period
persistence_driver: not stated for sand beaches (NOAA: among the easiest shorelines to clean; heavy oil is lifted off the lower beach by the rising tide)
scope_note: Rules and literature only until the sand-beach data model (owner decision 14 Nov 2026, built by another agent) is integrated; then the tier becomes experimental. Hook: decision_pipeline._beach_persistence_reference().
source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats; https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/Characteristic_Coastal_Habitats.pdf; ESI code: NOAA (2013) Shoreline Assessment Manual, 4th ed. (docs/reference/manual_shore_assess_aug2013.pdf), Table 1 p.27 and Appendix C p.C-3
status: Proposed (D36; descriptors transcribed by AI from NOAA text; owner to spot-check)
notes: NOAA's coarse-sand penetration (up to 25 cm) is on the same page; see ESI 4.

name: coarse-grained sand beach
oil_penetration_depth: up to about 25 cm in coarse-grained sand
burial_risk: rapid: within one day (NOAA p.22); Shoreline Assessment Manual: as rapid as one tidal cycle, to 60 cm or more, over 1 m possible if oil lands at the start of a depositional period
descriptor_source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats; https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/Characteristic_Coastal_Habitats.pdf; NOAA (2013) Shoreline Assessment Manual, 4th ed. (docs/reference/manual_shore_assess_aug2013.pdf), Table 1 p.27 and Appendix C pp.C-4 to C-5
scope_note: Same scope as ESI 3A: rules and literature only until the sand-beach data model is integrated.
source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats; https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/Characteristic_Coastal_Habitats.pdf; ESI code: NOAA (2013) Shoreline Assessment Manual, 4th ed. name: mixed sand and gravel beach
oil_penetration_depth: up to about 50 cm; behaves much like a sand beach if the sand fraction exceeds about 40 percent
burial_risk: may be deep at and above the high-tide line
persistence_driver: oil tends to persist at and above the high-tide line, particularly where the beach is only intermittently exposed to waves
asphalt_pavement_risk: yes: pavements of asphalted sediment can form in sheltered pockets if heavy oil accumulations are not removed
scope_note: Rules and literature only (owner decision 14 Nov 2026): no site-specific forecast and no data model for mixed sand and gravel.
source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats; https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/Characteristic_Coastal_Habitats.pdf; ESI code: NOAA (2013) Shoreline Assessment Manual, 4th ed. (docs/reference/manual_shore_assess_aug2013.pdf), Table 1 p.27 and Appendix C p.C-5
status: Proposed (D36; descriptors transcribed by AI from NOAA text; owner to spot-check)
notes: Permeability does not change the ESI class in this table; the older 'mixed_sediment plus high permeability' idiom for gravel is not used (use gravel_beach).

name: gravel beach
oil_penetration_depth: deep, because of high permeability (no depth stated)
burial_risk: rapid burial can occur at the high-tide and storm berms
persistence_driver: depth of routine reworking by waves; on exposed beaches oil can be pushed over the berms and persist above normal wave wash
asphalt_pavement_risk: yes: chronic sheening and asphalt pavements are likely along sheltered portions where accumulations are heavy
scope_note: Rules and literature only (owner decision 14 Nov 2026). Cobble is resolved here to ESI 6A: the Shoreline Assessment Manual describes ESI 6A sediments as pebbles to boulders (App. C p.C-6) and Table 1 as granules and pebbles.
source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats; https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/Characteristic_Coastal_Habitats.pdf; ESI code: NOAA (2013) Shoreline Assessment Manual, 4th ed. (docs/reference/manual_shore_assess_aug2013.pdf), Table 1 p.27 and Appendix C p.C-6
status: Proposed (D36; descriptors transcribed by AI from NOAA text; owner to spot-check)
notes: Decision D36: 'cobble' was treated as hard substrate by the screening rules and as a beach by the literature keywords; the pipeline now treats it as ESI 6A in both places. The FAST engine and other modules still read the raw string 'cobble' (hard substrate).

name: salt- to brackish-water marsh
oil_penetration_depth: medium to heavy oil does not readily penetrate fine sediment; light oil can penetrate the top few cm, up to 1 m in burrows and cracks
persistence_driver: oil adheres readily to vegetation; medium to heavy oil can pool on the surface or in burrows and root cavities
scope_note: Validated only for heavily oiled northern Gulf of Mexico marsh with an in-scope edge cell (existing F9 scope rule); experimental otherwise.
status: Proposed (D36; descriptors transcribed by AI from NOAA text; owner to spot-check)
notes: No NOAA ratings rows are transcribed for marsh; marsh screening stays with screening_rule.csv and treatment_conditions.csv.

name: mangrove (scrub-shrub wetland)
oil_penetration_depth: oil concentrates and penetrates into berm sediments or accumulated wrack and litter
persistence_driver: heavy and emulsified oil trapped in prop-root thickets; re-oiling from released residues
scope_note: Experimental: one-spill damage model (Bahia Las Minas) and mangrove_screening.csv.
source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats; https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/Characteristic_Coastal_Habitats.pdf; ESI code: NOAA (2013) Shoreline Assessment Manual, 4th ed. (docs/reference/manual_shore_assess_aug2013.pdf), Table 1 p.27 and Appendix C Table 1 p.27 (10D, scrub-shrub wetlands; mangroves)
status: Proposed (D36; descriptors transcribed by AI from NOAA text; owner to spot-check)

name: sheltered tidal flat (mudflat)
oil_penetration_depth: oil does not penetrate water-saturated sediment; may enter burrows and desiccation cracks
persistence_driver: oil accumulates at the high-tide line; mixing with suspended sediment can deposit contaminated sediment on the flat
scope_note: Rules and literature only. The marsh evidence class is applied to mudflat, as in the earlier code (existing ASSUMED grouping, unchanged).
source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats; https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/Characteristic_Coastal_Habitats.pdf; ESI code: NOAA (2013) Shoreline Assessment Manual, 4th ed. (docs/reference/manual_shore_assess_aug2013.pdf), Table 1 p.27 and Appendix C Table 1 p.27
status: Proposed (D36; descriptors transcribed by AI from NOAA text; owner to spot-check)
notes: Exposed tidal flats (ESI 7, NOAA p.37) are not separated.

name: peat shoreline
oil_penetration_depth: very low in frozen peat scarps; light oil can penetrate peat slurries; peat resists heavy oil
persistence_driver: high erosion rates (more than 1 m per year) give stranded oil a short residence time
scope_note: Rules and literature only. NOAA p.47: hot-water washing or even low-pressure flushing is not appropriate on peat.
source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats; https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/Characteristic_Coastal_Habitats.pdf; ESI code: NOAA (2013) Shoreline Assessment Manual, 4th ed. (docs/reference/manual_shore_assess_aug2013.pdf), Table 1 p.27 and Appendix C Table 1 p.27
status: Proposed (D36; descriptors transcribed by AI from NOAA text; owner to spot-check)
notes: The marsh evidence class is applied to peat, as in the earlier code.

name: inundated low-lying tundra
oil_penetration_depth: not stated (saturated peat; oil likely stays on the surface in summer)
persistence_driver: physical removal of medium to heavy oil is slow; oil can strand hundreds of metres inland in storm surges

name: exposed rocky shore
oil_penetration_depth: not stated (steep, hard surface; oil is held offshore by reflected waves)
persistence_driver: the most resistant oil remains as a patchy band at or above the high-tide line
scope_note: Rules and literature only. 'boulder' is kept with rocky shores as in the earlier code (ASSUMED; the Shoreline Assessment Manual lists boulders under both ESI 1C and ESI 6A).
source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats; https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/Characteristic_Coastal_Habitats.pdf; ESI code: NOAA (2013) Shoreline Assessment Manual, 4th ed. (docs/reference/manual_shore_assess_aug2013.pdf), Table 1 p.27 and Appendix C Table 1 p.27
status: Proposed (D36; descriptors transcribed by AI from NOAA text; owner to spot-check)
notes: Exposed versus sheltered is decided by wave_exposure (ASSUMED: low = sheltered, ESI 8A; moderate, high, very_high = exposed, ESI 1A). Wave-cut platforms (ESI 2A, NOAA p.20) and man-made structures are not separated.

name: sheltered rocky shore and scarp
oil_penetration_depth: not stated (oil adheres to dry, rough rock; wet lower intertidal rock stays clean)
persistence_driver: stranded oil persists because of the low-energy setting
